unmapped: Arms are pairs (i,j) in [K]x[L]; reward is product u_t(i)v_t(j) of independent latent row and column values (rank-1 mean matrix); individual values unobserved
The learner knows the number of columns L
settings.definition_quote: An instance of this problem is defined by a tuple $(K, L, P_\rowvar, P_\colvar)$, where $K$ is the number of rows, $L$ is the number of columns, $P_\rowvar$ is a probability distribution over a unit hypercube $[0, 1]^K$, and $P_\colvar$ is a probability distribution over a unit hypercube $[0, 1]^L$. ... At time $t$, it chooses arm $(\rnd{i}_t, \rnd{j}_t) \in [K] \times [L]$ ... and then observes $\rnd{u}_t(\rnd{i}_t) \rnd{v}_t(\rnd{j}_t)$, which is also its reward.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic rank-1 bandit with Bernoulli rows and columns (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are pairs (i,j) in [K]x[L]; reward is product of independent Bernoulli row and column variables (rank-1 mean matrix)
settings.definition_quote: We derive a gap-dependent lower bound on the family of rank-$1$ bandits where $P_\rowvar$ and $P_\colvar$ are products of independent Bernoulli variables, which are parameterized by their means $\bar{u}$ and $\bar{v}$, respectively.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic rank-1 bandit with Gaussian payoffs (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are pairs (i,j) in [K]x[L] with rank-1 mean matrix u(i)v(j), means in [0,1], Gaussian payoffs with common variance sigma^2
settings.definition_quote: We still assume that the means are in $[0,1]$, as before. We also assume that all payoffs have a common variance $\sigma^2>0$.

symbols.mu_avg: min of the average row mean and average column mean, mu = min{(1/K) sum_i u(i), (1/L) sum_j v(j)}
symbols.S_u: sum over all rows i of 1/barDelta^u_i, where barDelta^u_i = Delta^u_i, or Delta^v_min if Delta^u_i = 0
symbols.S_v: sum over all columns j of 1/barDelta^v_j, where barDelta^v_j = Delta^v_j, or Delta^u_min if Delta^v_j = 0

conditions: row and column values in [0,1], drawn independently
n >= 3 (used in the proof: log n >= 1)

source.label: thm:upper bound
source.quote: The expected $n$-step regret of $\bilinucb$ is bounded as R(n) \leq \frac{1}{\mu^2} \left(\sum_{i = 1}^K \frac{384}{\bar{\Delta}^\rowvar_i} + \sum_{j = 1}^L \frac{384}{\bar{\Delta}^\colvar_j}\right) \log n + 3 (K + L), where \bar{\Delta}^\rowvar_i = \Delta^\rowvar_i + \I{\Delta^\rowvar_i = 0} \Delta^\colvar_{\min}, \bar{\Delta}^\colvar_j = \Delta^\colvar_j + \I{\Delta^\colvar_j = 0} \Delta^\rowvar_{\min}.

results.notes: The regret is defined as the expectation of the instantaneous stochastic regret against the fixed optimal pair, which equals pseudo-regret. The paper summarises it as O((K+L)(1/mu^2)(1/Delta) log n).

symbols.LB_row: sum over suboptimal rows i of (u(i*)v(j*) - u(i)v(j*)) / kl(u(i)v(j*), u(i*)v(j*))
symbols.LB_col: sum over suboptimal columns j of (u(i*)v(j*) - u(i*)v(j)) / kl(u(i*)v(j), u(i*)v(j*))

conditions: uniformly efficient algorithm: R(n) = o(n^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1) and all instances
identifiability: 0 < d(u(i)v(j), u(i')v(j')) < infinity for distinct pairs (appendix)

source.label: thm:lower bound
source.quote: For any problem $(\bar{u}, \bar{v}) \in [0, 1]^K \times [0, 1]^L$ with a unique best arm and any uniformly efficient algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ whose regret is $R(n)$, \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n)}{\log n} \geq \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \set{i^\ast}} \frac{\bar{u}(i^\ast) \bar{v}(j^\ast) - \bar{u}(i) \bar{v}(j^\ast)}{d(\bar{u}(i) \bar{v}(j^\ast), \bar{u}(i^\ast) \bar{v}(j^\ast))} + \sum_{j \in [L] \setminus \set{j^\ast}} ...

results.notes: Proved with change-of-measure arguments (Graves-Lai / Kaufmann et al.). I mapped 'uniformly efficient' to uniformly_good.

symbols.u_star: mean of the optimal row u(i*)
symbols.v_star: mean of the optimal column v(j*)

conditions: uniformly efficient algorithm: R(n) = o(n^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1)
Gaussian row and column rewards with common variance sigma^2

source.label: cor:gaussLB
source.quote: For any $(\bar{u}, \bar{v}) \in [0, 1]^K \times [0, 1]^L$ with a unique optimal action and any uniformly efficient algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ whose regret is $R(n)$, assuming Gaussian row and column rewards with common variance $\sigma^2$, \liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R(n)}{\log(n)}\geq \frac{2\sigma^2}{\bar{v}(j^*)}\sum_{i\in[K]\setminus \{i^*\}}\frac{1}{\Delta^\rowvar_i}+ \frac{2\sigma^2}{\bar{u}(i^*)}\sum_{j\in[L]\setminus \{j^*\}}\frac{1}{\Delta^\colvar_j}.

results.notes: The paper says the Theorem 2 proof is 'repeated with minor differences'. The theorem does not state whether sigma is known to the learner.
